claims.text: The as-cast or minimally processed lightweight high-entropy alloy has a largely chemically disordered, multi-principal-element microstructure.
Post-casting heat treatment can increase nanoscale chemical ordering without changing the alloy's overall composition.

Increasing nanoscale chemical ordering enables lightweight high-entropy alloys to retain low density while simultaneously improving mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Enhanced chemical ordering increases local chemical and structural heterogeneity.
Nanoscale chemical ordering produces controlled lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion reinforces the alloy matrix and increases mechanical strength.
Enhanced nanoscale ordering directs the formation of a coherent, self-limiting, and adherent oxide film.
The oxide film formed in the ordered state is potentially self-healing.
A stable protective oxide layer improves corrosion resistance.
A stable protective oxide layer improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
More highly ordered samples will have greater yield strength than compositionally identical, less-ordered samples.
More highly ordered samples will show greater corrosion resistance, including higher passive-film impedance, than less-ordered samples.
More highly ordered samples will form more stable high-temperature oxide films than less-ordered samples.
Excessive heat treatment can produce significant grain coarsening.
Inadequate or excessive heat treatment that produces an undesirable grain structure can diminish corrosion resistance and physical properties.
Excessive heat treatment can cause phase segregation or loss of nanoscale ordering.
Loss of nanoscale ordering disrupts coherent oxide-film formation.
Loss of nanoscale ordering decreases lattice-distortion strengthening.
